recommended_first_journey.rationale: Personal Current Account Opening is the foundational entry point for the bank's retail relationship. It simultaneously exercises onboarding (CAP-001.01), identity verification and KYC (CAP-005.01), and digital channel provisioning (CAP-007). Modelling this journey first establishes the canonical patterns for eligibility checks, AML screening, document capture, and account activation that recur in almost every other journey. It also surfaces the cross-capability integration points — between the core banking ledger, the compliance platform, and the digital front-end — that must be resolved before downstream journeys can be designed reliably.

journeys.name: Personal Current Account Opening
journeys.description: A retail customer applies for and is onboarded to a personal current account, including identity verification, KYC screening, and activation of digital banking access. This is the primary retail onboarding journey and the entry point for most subsequent personal banking relationships.
journeys.priority_rationale: Regulatory obligation to perform KYC and AML checks before account activation; directly impacts onboarding conversion and revenue. Foundational for all downstream retail journeys.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer submits application online, provides identity documents, system performs automated KYC and sanctions screening, account is approved, IBAN/sort-code-account-number allocated, debit card ordered, and digital banking credentials provisioned — all within the same session.

journeys.name: Faster Payment Initiation
journeys.description: A retail or business customer initiates a domestic Faster Payment from their account, with real-time fraud and sanctions screening before the payment is submitted to the Faster Payments Scheme. Core to daily active usage of the bank's payment services.
journeys.priority_rationale: Faster Payments are subject to PSR regulatory obligations; real-time sanctions screening is a legal requirement. Highest-volume transaction type for retail customers.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer enters payee details and amount, system performs real-time sanctions and fraud checks, payment instruction is submitted to the Faster Payments Scheme, funds are debited immediately, and the customer receives a transaction confirmation with a Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference.

journeys.name: Mortgage Application
journeys.description: A retail customer applies for a residential mortgage, triggering affordability assessment, credit risk evaluation, property valuation, and offer generation. One of the highest-value and most regulated retail lending journeys.
journeys.priority_rationale: MCOB regulatory requirements, significant credit risk exposure, and high customer lifetime value make this a board-level priority. Errors in affordability assessment carry PRA and FCA enforcement risk.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer completes a digital mortgage application with income and expenditure data, the system runs an automated affordability and credit risk assessment, a Decision in Principle is issued, a full application is submitted, a valuation is instructed, and a formal mortgage offer is generated within the regulatory 10-business-day target.

journeys.name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing
journeys.description: A Money Laundering Reporting Officer or nominated compliance officer files an internal Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) and, where appropriate, a SAR with the National Crime Agency. Core compliance workflow with strict regulatory timelines.
journeys.priority_rationale: Failure to file a SAR within the required timeline constitutes a criminal offence under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002. Regulatory critical with no margin for error.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Compliance officer receives an alert or identifies suspicious activity, raises an internal SAR with supporting evidence, the MLRO reviews and approves, the SAR is submitted to NCA via the SARs Online portal, a consent or no-consent response is recorded, and the case is closed with full audit trail.

journeys.name: Business Account Opening
journeys.description: A business customer (sole trader or SME) applies to open a business current account, with enhanced KYC covering Ultimate Beneficial Ownership verification alongside standard AML checks.
journeys.priority_rationale: UBO verification is a legal requirement under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017; business onboarding is a key revenue entry point for commercial banking.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Business submits application with Companies House registration details, directors provide identity documents, system performs automated UBO lookup and AML screening, account is approved by a relationship manager, sort code and account number are allocated, and online business banking access is provisioned.

journeys.name: International Wire Transfer
journeys.description: A business customer initiates a SWIFT international wire transfer, triggering correspondent banking routing, real-time sanctions screening, and FX conversion if the destination currency differs from the account currency.
journeys.priority_rationale: SWIFT cross-border payments are subject to OFAC and HM Treasury sanctions obligations; mandatory payer/payee data requirements under the Wire Transfer Regulation. High commercial value.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer enters beneficiary IBAN, BIC, and payment details; system validates mandatory Wire Transfer Regulation fields, performs real-time sanctions screening, applies FX rate if needed, routes the payment through the correspondent banking network via SWIFT MT103, and delivers a tracking reference.

journeys.name: Credit Card Application
journeys.description: A retail customer applies for a credit card, including an automated credit risk assessment, credit limit assignment, and card issuance with immediate virtual card provisioning.
journeys.priority_rationale: Credit cards are a major retail revenue product; FCA Consumer Duty requires affordability checks are robust and lending is sustainable.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer submits an in-app credit card application, the system performs an automated credit bureau check and affordability assessment, a credit limit is assigned, the application is approved in real time, a virtual card is immediately provisioned to the customer's digital wallet, and a physical card is dispatched.

journeys.name: Business Loan Origination
journeys.description: An SME customer applies for a term loan, triggering financial spreading, credit risk assessment, covenant setting, and credit committee approval before facility letters are issued.
journeys.priority_rationale: Business lending is a primary revenue driver for commercial banking; PRA credit risk rules require documented affordability and covenant frameworks.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Relationship manager collects financial statements, the system performs financial spreading and automated credit scoring, a credit application is submitted to the credit committee, approval is granted, facility letter is generated and countersigned, and the loan is booked on the core system with covenant monitoring activated.

journeys.name: Open Banking Consent and Payment
journeys.description: A third-party provider initiates a payment or data-sharing request on behalf of a customer under the Open Banking / PSD2 framework, requiring strong customer authentication and explicit consent capture.
journeys.priority_rationale: PSD2 and FCA Open Banking rules make AISP/PISP access a regulatory obligation; non-compliance carries FCA enforcement risk and CMA remediation orders.
journeys.happy_path_summary: TPP redirects customer to the bank's authorisation endpoint, customer completes SCA (biometric or OTP), consents to the specific data scope or payment, the bank issues an access token or executes the payment instruction, and a consent record is persisted for audit purposes.

journeys.name: Card Transaction Authorisation
journeys.description: A retail customer presents a debit or credit card for payment at a point of sale or online, triggering real-time authorisation, fraud scoring, and balance/limit checks before the transaction is approved or declined.
journeys.priority_rationale: Card authorisation is the highest-volume real-time interaction in retail banking; fraud losses and false-positive declines both carry significant financial and reputational cost.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Merchant acquirer sends an ISO 8583 authorisation request, the bank's card processing platform checks available balance or credit limit, runs a real-time fraud score, approves the transaction, posts an authorisation hold, and returns an approval code to the merchant within 200 ms.

journeys.name: Direct Debit Setup
journeys.description: A retail customer authorises a new Direct Debit instruction for a payee, which is validated against the Bacs scheme rules and stored for future collection cycles.
journeys.priority_rationale: Direct Debits underpin subscription and utility bill payments; Bacs scheme compliance is mandatory and errors trigger refund obligations under the Direct Debit Guarantee.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer submits a new Direct Debit mandate, the bank validates the service user number and sort code via Bacs, stores the mandate, sends an advance notice to the customer, and the mandate is ready for collection by the originator on the agreed date.

journeys.name: Standing Order Management
journeys.description: A retail customer creates, amends, or cancels a standing order instruction for recurring fixed payments, with the bank managing the payment schedule against the Faster Payments or Bacs rail.
journeys.priority_rationale: Standing orders are a high-volume, customer-initiated payment type; errors in scheduling or cancellation processing generate significant complaints and potential regulatory censure.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer sets up a standing order via online banking specifying payee, amount, frequency, and start date; the system stores the instruction, schedules executions against the payment calendar, and sends confirmation. Amendments or cancellations are applied immediately and confirmed.

journeys.name: Fraud Alert Investigation
journeys.description: A fraud analyst investigates an automated fraud alert triggered on a customer account, decides whether to block the account and contact the customer, and resolves the case with appropriate remediation.
journeys.priority_rationale: Fraud losses are a direct P&L impact; PSR APP fraud reimbursement rules create mandatory reimbursement obligations; timely investigation is required to limit customer harm.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Fraud system raises an alert on anomalous transaction behaviour, analyst reviews the alert in the case management tool, contacts the customer for verification, determines the transaction is fraudulent, blocks the card, initiates a chargeback, and closes the case with a recovery recommendation.

journeys.name: Investment Portfolio Review
journeys.description: A wealth management customer reviews their investment portfolio with a relationship manager, receives a suitability assessment, and is presented with rebalancing recommendations aligned to their risk profile.
journeys.priority_rationale: MiFID II suitability requirements mandate periodic portfolio reviews; wealth management is a high-margin business but serves a smaller customer segment.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer schedules a portfolio review, the system generates a pre-meeting suitability report and performance summary, the relationship manager discusses rebalancing options, the customer approves a rebalancing instruction, and trades are executed with a post-trade confirmation sent to the customer.

journeys.name: Trade Finance Letter of Credit
journeys.description: A corporate customer applies for a documentary Letter of Credit to support an international trade transaction, requiring credit assessment, document checking, and SWIFT LC message issuance.
journeys.priority_rationale: Letters of Credit are a specialist but high-value trade finance product; UCP 600 compliance and sanctions screening of beneficiary and goods are mandatory.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Corporate submits an LC application with trade documents, credit team assesses the risk and approves the facility, the bank issues the LC via SWIFT MT700 to the beneficiary's correspondent bank, the exporter presents compliant documents, the bank checks documents against LC terms, and payment is released.

journeys.name: FX Spot Trade
journeys.description: A treasury or corporate banking customer executes a spot foreign exchange trade, receiving a real-time rate, confirming the deal, and settling on T+2 through the bank's FX platform.
journeys.priority_rationale: FX trading supports corporate clients hedging currency exposure; FX Global Code compliance and best execution obligations apply under MiFID II.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Trader requests a spot rate for a currency pair, the system returns a real-time streaming quote, the trader accepts the rate within the validity window, the deal is booked and confirmed via SWIFT MT300, nostro accounts are updated, and settlement instructions are dispatched for T+2 settlement.

journeys.name: Regulatory Return Submission
journeys.description: A regulatory reporting officer compiles and submits a mandatory PRA or FCA regulatory return (e.g., COREP, FINREP, or Gabriel return), including internal sign-off, data validation, and submission through the regulator's portal.
journeys.priority_rationale: Regulatory returns carry statutory submission deadlines; late or inaccurate submissions attract PRA/FCA enforcement action and potential public censure.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Reporting system aggregates source data from the core banking and risk platforms, pre-populates the return template, the regulatory reporting officer reviews and validates the data, a senior sign-off is obtained, the return is submitted via the regulator's portal before the deadline, and a submission receipt is archived.

journeys.name: Merchant Onboarding
journeys.description: A new merchant applies to accept card payments through the bank's acquiring services, triggering KYC, business verification, scheme membership checks, and terminal provisioning.
journeys.priority_rationale: Merchant acquiring is a growing revenue line; card scheme rules (Visa/Mastercard) mandate KYC and risk assessment before merchant activation to prevent card fraud laundering.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Merchant submits an online application with business registration and bank details, the system performs KYC and scheme-mandated risk checks, a merchant ID is assigned, terminal or payment gateway credentials are provisioned, a welcome pack is sent, and the merchant is activated for acquiring within 48 hours.

journeys.name: Insurance Product Purchase
journeys.description: A retail customer purchases an insurance product (e.g., home insurance) through the bank's bancassurance channel, with needs assessment, product recommendation, and policy issuance.
journeys.priority_rationale: Bancassurance is a secondary revenue stream; FCA Consumer Duty requirements for suitability and fair value assessments apply to insurance distribution.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer completes a digital needs assessment, the system presents suitable insurance products with key features and pricing, the customer selects a product and pays the premium, a policy document is issued electronically, and coverage begins on the selected start date.

journeys.name: Customer Complaint Handling
journeys.description: A retail customer raises a formal complaint, which is triaged, investigated, resolved within FCA timelines, and reported in the bank's complaints MI. Includes potential referral to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
journeys.priority_rationale: DISP rules require complaints to be resolved within 8 weeks; high complaint volumes or systemic issues attract FCA supervisory attention and potential Section 166 reviews.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer raises a complaint via any channel, the case is logged and triaged by the complaints team, a case handler investigates and contacts the customer within 5 working days, a final response letter is issued within 8 weeks with any appropriate redress, and the case is closed and reported in regulatory MI.

journeys.name: Overdraft Limit Review
journeys.description: A relationship manager or automated system reviews a retail customer's overdraft limit, assesses affordability under FCA overdraft rules, and applies a limit increase, reduction, or withdrawal.
journeys.priority_rationale: FCA overdraft pricing rules require annual affordability reviews; failure to identify customers in financial difficulty creates Consumer Duty and CONC regulatory risk.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Automated affordability model runs against updated credit bureau data, flags customers whose limit should change, a relationship manager reviews the recommendation for high-risk cases, the limit change is applied, the customer is notified with a clear explanation, and the review is logged for regulatory reporting.

journeys.name: Savings Account Interest Calculation
journeys.description: The bank's core banking system calculates and applies interest to retail savings accounts on the scheduled calculation date, including tiered rate logic and ISA allowance tracking.
journeys.priority_rationale: Interest calculation accuracy is a core banking obligation; errors create customer harm, complaints, and FCA BCOBS regulatory risk. Largely automated but high impact.
journeys.happy_path_summary: At the scheduled calculation date, the core banking engine calculates interest using the prevailing tiered rate for each savings account, applies the credit to the account balance, updates the annual interest summary, sends the customer a statement entry, and reports ISA subscriptions to HMRC.

journeys.name: GDPR Subject Access Request
journeys.description: A retail customer submits a Subject Access Request under UK GDPR, triggering a systematic search across all data stores, collation of personal data, and delivery of the response pack within the statutory 30-day deadline.
journeys.priority_rationale: UK GDPR SAR obligations carry ICO enforcement risk for late or incomplete responses, but volume is low relative to other journeys. Operationally important but not a daily-volume flow.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Customer submits a SAR via any channel, identity is verified, a case is opened, data teams search across core banking, CRM, communications, and archive systems, personal data is collated and redacted for third-party information, and a complete response pack is delivered to the customer within 30 calendar days.

journeys.name: Annual Stress Test Execution
journeys.description: Risk and finance teams run the annual PRA stress test, including scenario modelling across credit, market, and liquidity risk, capital adequacy projections, and submission of results to the PRA.
journeys.priority_rationale: PRA stress testing is a statutory requirement but runs annually; the journey is long-running and managed by specialist teams rather than a daily operational flow.
journeys.happy_path_summary: PRA publishes the stress test scenario, the bank's risk and finance teams load scenarios into the stress testing platform, run capital projections across all portfolios, review outputs with senior management and the Board Risk Committee, produce a management actions overlay, and submit results to the PRA within the prescribed timeline.

journeys.name: CDD Periodic Review
journeys.description: The compliance team conducts a scheduled periodic Customer Due Diligence review for an existing business or high-risk customer, refreshing KYC information and re-screening against current sanctions and PEP lists.
journeys.priority_rationale: MLR 2017 requires periodic CDD reviews commensurate with risk; this is an ongoing operational compliance task rather than a revenue-generating journey.
journeys.happy_path_summary: The CDD system flags a customer as due for periodic review, the compliance team contacts the customer for updated information and documents, the refreshed data is re-screened against sanctions and PEP lists, the risk rating is reassessed, and the CDD record is updated with the next review date recorded.

journeys.name: Correspondent Bank Relationship Setup
journeys.description: The bank's transaction banking team onboards a new correspondent banking relationship, including enhanced due diligence on the respondent bank, SWIFT BIC registration, and nostro account setup.
journeys.priority_rationale: FATF Recommendation 13 requires enhanced due diligence for correspondent relationships; this is a low-frequency but high-risk setup activity that enables international payment flows.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Transaction banking team identifies a new correspondent bank, completes an enhanced due diligence questionnaire and Wolfsberg correspondent banking due diligence process, the compliance team approves the relationship, SWIFT BIC is registered, a nostro account is opened, and test payment flows are confirmed before go-live.

journeys.name: Branch Cash Management
journeys.description: A branch operations team manages daily vault cash balancing, orders cash replenishment from the cash centre, and processes customer cash transactions against the branch till system.
journeys.priority_rationale: Branch cash management is operationally important for physical branches but declining in volume with digital adoption; low strategic priority relative to digital journeys.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Branch opens the vault, till balances are verified against the previous day's close, cash transactions are processed and posted to customer accounts in real time, a cash order is placed with the cash centre when levels fall below the minimum threshold, and the branch closes with an end-of-day till reconciliation.

journeys.name: Senior Manager Oversight Dashboard
journeys.description: A Senior Manager (SMF holder) accesses a real-time executive dashboard providing oversight across all capability domains — risk metrics, customer metrics, operational KPIs, and regulatory alerts — to fulfil their SMCR prescribed responsibilities.
journeys.priority_rationale: SMCR individual accountability requirements create a regulatory need for Senior Managers to evidence oversight; the dashboard supports this but is a reporting journey rather than a transactional one.
journeys.happy_path_summary: Senior Manager logs in with MFA-protected credentials, the dashboard aggregates live data from risk, finance, operations, and compliance platforms, presents a structured view of the bank's health across all capability domains, flags any breaches of risk appetite or regulatory thresholds, and provides drill-down to underlying metrics for each area of prescribed responsibility.
